// Why the commission model is broken

Every host who has listed on Booking.com knows the feeling of watching a booking confirmation arrive and immediately calculating how much of it belongs to the platform. At 15% average commission, one in every six rand of every booking goes to Booking.com before a single operational cost is counted. At 20% — which Preferred Partner listings with payment processing can reach — one in five rand disappears.

This has been the accommodation industry's accepted cost of doing business for two decades. It does not have to be. The question is not whether OTA platforms provide value — they do, particularly for new guest acquisition and international visibility. The question is whether that value justifies the ongoing cost at the percentage they charge, year after year, on every booking a repeat guest makes.

TripSpace Global is built on a different model. R450 per month. No commission per booking. Hosts keep 100% of every rand a guest pays. For a property with ten bookings per month averaging R3,000 each, that is R30,000 in monthly booking revenue — all of it reaching the host. On Booking.com at 15%, R4,500 of that R30,000 goes to the platform every single month.

What TripSpace Global actually is

// Chapter 02 — The platform explained

TripSpace Global is a commission-free travel marketplace that lists accommodation, car rentals, safari experiences, and activities worldwide. It is not a South Africa-only platform — it operates globally, with particular strength in the South African market where the commission burden of major OTAs falls heaviest relative to average nightly rates.

The model works as follows: hosts pay R450 per month to list. That flat fee covers unlimited bookings — whether a property generates two bookings per month or two hundred, the platform cost stays the same. For larger properties, the fee scales to R450 per five rooms monthly. A ten-room guesthouse pays R900 per month. A twenty-room boutique hotel pays R1,800 per month. At any revenue level above approximately R6,000 per year in bookings, TripSpace is cheaper than Booking.com.

The platform supports direct host-to-guest relationships. Unlike Booking.com, where guest contact is mediated through the platform's messaging system and email addresses are withheld until close to check-in, TripSpace allows hosts to build genuine relationships with their guests — which is what converts a one-time booking into a repeat direct booking.

A guest who books through Booking.com belongs to Booking.com. A guest who books through TripSpace Global belongs to the host. That distinction compounds over years of operation into the most valuable asset a hospitality business can own — a loyal direct booking database.

The strategy — use both platforms correctly

// Chapter 03 — How to use TripSpace alongside Booking.com

The honest recommendation is not to abandon Booking.com entirely. Its reach — 500 million registered users, dominant international search presence — is genuinely valuable for new guest acquisition. The strategy is to use each platform for what it does best.

Use Booking.com to acquire new guests. Its volume and international visibility are real advantages, particularly for guests who do not know the local market. Pay the 15% on that first booking as an acquisition cost — the same way a business pays for advertising to attract a new customer.

Use TripSpace Global to retain those guests. Every guest who books through Booking.com and returns for a second booking should be encouraged to book direct — through TripSpace or the host's own channel. That second booking costs the host R450/month (shared across all bookings) instead of 15% per transaction. Over a guest lifetime of five to ten stays, the savings compound significantly.

For South African hosts specifically — where average nightly rates are lower relative to the commission percentages than in European or North American markets — the math is particularly compelling. A R800/night guesthouse room generating R112,000 per year in bookings pays R16,800 per year to Booking.com at 15%, versus R5,400 to TripSpace. The R11,400 annual difference is meaningful money for an independent operator.

Who TripSpace Global is built for

// Chapter 04 — The right fit

TripSpace Global is particularly well suited to independent accommodation operators in South Africa and Africa who are generating consistent bookings but want to reduce their OTA dependency over time. The flat-fee model rewards hosts with higher occupancy — the more bookings a property generates, the cheaper TripSpace becomes per booking relative to a percentage-based platform.

It is also well suited to new properties that want to build a direct booking channel from day one rather than becoming entirely dependent on OTA traffic. Starting with both Booking.com and TripSpace simultaneously allows a new property to use OTA volume to build occupancy while developing the direct booking habit with guests from the beginning.

Safari operators, car rental companies, and activity providers in Southern Africa have an additional reason to consider TripSpace — the platform covers the full travel experience, not just accommodation. A safari lodge that also offers game drives, transfers, and equipment can list all of those services under one platform rather than managing multiple OTA relationships across different categories.

How much does TripSpace Global cost compared to Booking.com?
TripSpace Global charges R450 per month (R5,400 per year) regardless of booking volume. Booking.com charges 10-25% commission on every booking — averaging 15% globally. For a property earning R300,000 per year, TripSpace saves R39,600 annually versus Booking.com at 15% commission.
Can I list on TripSpace Global and Booking.com at the same time?
Yes — and this is the recommended strategy. Use Booking.com for international reach and new guest acquisition. Use TripSpace Global to convert repeat guests to zero-commission direct bookings. Every guest who books direct on their second stay saves you 15% commission on that and all future bookings.
What types of listings does TripSpace Global accept?
TripSpace Global accepts accommodation (BnBs, guesthouses, holiday homes, hotels, lodges), car rentals, safari and wildlife experiences, and activities. It is a full travel marketplace — not accommodation only. Visit tripspaceglobal.com to list.
Is TripSpace Global available outside South Africa?
Yes. TripSpace Global operates worldwide. The platform lists accommodation, car rentals, safaris, and activities globally. It is positioned as a global commission-free travel marketplace.
